data.gender_notes: Jaquenette is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jaquenette is a name with a beautiful and elegant meaning. It is derived from the French name Jacqueline, which comes from the name Jacque, meaning 'supplanter'. However, Jaquenette adds the feminine suffix -ette, which means 'little'. The name as a whole conveys the idea of a graceful goddess or a little supplanter. The name Jaquenette carries the meaning “Graceful Goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Jaquenette usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: ג'קנט
in_hebrew.meaning: תחליף אלוהים, אלוהים יחליף, אלוהים יגאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ג'קנט הוא גרסה צרפתית של השם העברי 'יעקב', שפירושו 'תחליף אלוהים' או 'אלוהים יחליף'. השם נגזר מהמילה העברית 'עקב', שפירושו 'עקב' או 'תחת'. בהקשר המקראי, השם יעקב ניתן לבן התאומים השני של יצחק ואביגיל, שיצא מהרחם אחר אחיו תאומים, עשו. השם ג'קנט משמש כגרסה נוצרית של השם, המשקפת את הקשר בין השם העברי למסורת הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Ζακενέτ
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Ζακενέτ εἰς ἡ Γαλλικὴ παραλλαγὴ τοῦ Εβραϊκοῦ ὀνόματος 'Ιακώβ', ὃ σημαίνει 'Αντικατάστασις Θεοῦ' ἤ 'Θεὸς ἀντικαταστήσει'. Τὸ ὄνομα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὸ Εβραϊκὸ λόγο 'עקב', ὃ σημαίνει 'εὐκίνησις' ἤ 'κάτω μέρος'. Στο βιβλικό πλαίσιο, τὸ ὄνομα Ιακώβ δόθηκε στὸ δεύτερο δίδυμο παιδί τοῦ Ισαακ καὶ τῆς Αβρααμ, ποῦ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπὸ τὴν κοιλίαν μετὰ τὸν ἀδελφὸν του Ἠσαῦ. Τὸ ὄνομα Ζακενέτ χρησιμοποείται ὡς Χριστιανικὴ παραλλαγὴ τοῦ ονόματος, ἀνακλαστικὸ τῆς συνδέσεως μεταξὺ τοῦ Εβραϊκοῦ ονόματος καὶ τῆς Χριστιανικῆς παραδόσεως.

in_latin.name: Jaquenette
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Jaquenette est forma gallica nominis hebraici 'Jacob', quod significat 'Deus substituet' vel 'Deus mutabit'. Nomen derivatur a voce hebraica 'עקב', quae significat 'calcaneus' vel 'substituere'. In contextu biblico, nomen Jacob datum est filio secundo gemino Isaac et Rebekkae, qui egressus est de utero post fratrem suum Esau. Nomen Jaquenette adhibetur ut forma christiana nominis, reflectens nexum inter nomen hebraicum et traditionem christianam.

in_english.name: Jaquenette
in_english.meaning: God will substitute, God will replace
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jaquenette is a French variant of the Hebrew name 'Jacob', which means 'God will substitute' or 'God will replace'. Derived from the Hebrew word 'עקב' (e'qeb), meaning 'heel' or 'to follow', the name has significant biblical roots. In the Bible, Jacob was the second twin son of Isaac and Rebecca, and his name reflects his birth circumstances, as he emerged from the womb grasping the heel of his twin brother Esau. The name Jaquenette carries this rich biblical heritage into Christian tradition, symbolizing divine providence and the concept of replacement or substitution. Historically, the name Jaquenette has been used in Christian cultures to signify faith and divine plan.
